title: Safe measuring, dilution and dispensing demonstration
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain hazards and scope boundaries for controlled dilution and dispensing
Demonstrate an authorised procedure with appropriate controls

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Confirm whether dilution is permitted
instruction.body: Many products are ready to use. Only dilute a concentrate when the manufacturer explicitly specifies it and the workplace authorises the task. Confirm the required ratio, units, temperature, application method and contact time.

instruction.heading: Prepare the dispensing station
instruction.body: Use a designated ventilated area, suitable PPE, stable measuring equipment, a compatible labelled container and spill controls. Keep food and personal items away. Check that the container is clean and not holding unknown residues.

instruction.heading: Calculate using an example
instruction.body: For an explicitly authorised 1:20 concentrate-to-water ratio and a final 2.1 L batch, one part concentrate plus twenty parts water equals 21 parts: 100 mL concentrate and 2,000 mL water. Ratios are not universal; verify whether the label specifies concentrate-to-water or concentrate-to-total before calculating.

instruction.heading: Dispense without exposure
instruction.body: Follow the manufacturer’s order of addition, use accurate measures, avoid splashes and never improvise with drinking cups. Close the original container promptly. Do not decant into beverage bottles.

instruction.heading: Label, verify and store
instruction.body: Apply required product identity, concentration, preparation/expiry details and hazard information. Check the mixture against the instruction before release. Clean the station and record who prepared it. If a calculation or label is uncertain, do not use the mixture.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Confirm the product label specifies dilution and the workplace authorises the task before mixing anything.
Confirm the ratio basis, units, temperature, application method and contact time from the label before calculating.
Set up a ventilated dispensing area with suitable PPE, stable measuring equipment, a clean labelled container and spill controls.
Calculate the batch only once the ratio basis is confirmed, and check the figures against the label.
Add the components in the manufacturer's order of addition, avoid splashes, and close the original container promptly.
Label the mixture with its product identity, concentration, preparation and expiry details, and its hazard information.
Check the mixture against the instruction before release, and do not use it if the calculation or label is uncertain.
Clean the station and record who prepared the mixture.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: Dilution is carried out only where the label specifies it and the task is authorised.
The ratio basis is confirmed against the label before any calculation is made.
The dispensing area is ventilated, PPE is worn, and the container is clean and free of unknown residue.
Each mixture carries its product identity, concentration and preparation details and is checked before release.
summary: Dilution happens only when the manufacturer specifies it and the workplace authorises the task.
The ratio basis is checked against the label before any calculation, and the worked example shows 100 mL of concentrate with 2,000 mL of water for a 2.1 litre batch at 1:20.
Mixtures are labelled and checked before release, and an uncertain calculation or label means the mixture is not used.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen when the dilution ratio for a mixture is uncertain?
options: Dilute by eye, since the mixture is probably similar to the last one used
Use the strongest mix to be safe on every surface, in every room and the hall
Stop and confirm with the supervisor or the label before diluting or using the mixture
Guess a ratio, then check it after cleaning the surface, the room and the hall

knowledgeChecks.question: What evidence shows a dilution was prepared and labelled correctly?
options: A measuring cup used afterwards to hold a drink at the desk today too
An unlabelled bottle filled with the mixture for later use in the room
A verbal record that the mixture was made correctly by the worker today
A label-checked mixture, with preparation details recorded and the station cleaned

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a client's request for a different dilution be handled?
options: Decline to mix or dispense it, and refer the request for approval
Mix a stronger batch to meet the client's request
Dispense it into a clean spray bottle that is kept at the bench
Use a different ratio that the client suggests

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a concentrate be diluted, according to the lesson?
options: When the client asks for it
When the manufacturer explicitly specifies it and the workplace authorises the task
